title: Hands-on: Three Operator Cases
points: Run voltage support, service restoration and cyber response in Classroom Labs
120 minutes · one CPU notebook · three short exercises
IEEE ComSoc theme / Run, change, check and explain
note: Open Classroom Labs before the workshop. Participants will run fresh numerical calculations and inspect clearly labeled archived model replies. Use the same notebook for all three cases. If devices are limited, work in pairs: one person runs the cells while the other checks the evidence.

title: Open one notebook for all three cases
points: Open Classroom Labs using the source link below or the website’s first Colab button.
Save a copy in Drive so you can keep your parameter changes and outputs.
note: Open https://alaaselim-sudo.github.io/GridGuard-Agentic-AI-Tutorials/#notebooks and choose the first notebook, Classroom Labs. The LangGraph and trace notebooks are separate companions. Keep the slides in one tab and Classroom Labs in another.

action_link.label: Open Classroom Labs in Google Colab

title: Connect a CPU and run the setup cell
points: Connect a standard CPU runtime. Run “Set up Google Colab (CPU)” and wait for Ready.
Setup retrieves the supporting data, saved weights and records. It installs the required packages.
note: For a paced workshop, run the setup cell first, then run each named lesson cell when prompted. Runtime > Run all also works, but it reveals later outputs before the prediction questions. The default route needs no GPU, API key or model download. If setup stops, reconnect the runtime and rerun setup before starting L0.

title: Find cells by L label, not by cell number
points: Use the section headings L0 through L12 to find the next task.
Run a whole code cell with its play button or Shift+Enter. Later cells use earlier variables.
note: The added Colab setup cells changed the numerical cell positions. Use the L headings and stable cell IDs to find the same source in Colab, Jupyter and these slides. A slide shows only the relevant code fragment. Students should run the complete matching notebook cell.

title: Run L0: choose the classroom route
points: Keep both switches False. The class uses fresh linear-model calculations and saved model replies.
If the data check fails, rerun the setup cell before continuing.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L0–L1; cells classroom-002 and classroom-004.
note: Run all of L0 to import the helpers, configure the plots and initialize the timing record. Keep RUN_OPENDSS=False and RUN_LOCAL_LLAMA=False. These settings skip the optional full-feeder OpenDSS route and local model service. They do not make the calculations prerecorded: L2 and L4 through L9 run fresh numerical calculations or checks, while L12 checks the evidence binding and simulated readback.

title: Know which evidence you are reading
points: FRESH: calculated now. SAVED POLICY: old weights used for a new proposal.
ARCHIVED ACTUAL LLM: a previously recorded reply, with its original input and timing.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L0–L1; cells classroom-002 and classroom-004.
note: The diagram shows responsibilities. Ordinary Python functions perform the engineering calculations; this notebook does not run through LangGraph. A model reply remains an archived event when displayed today. A language model does not replace the power-flow solver, MILP or state estimator.
caption: Teaching diagram of the model or check used at this notebook step.

title: Run L1: does old evidence still match?
points: Run the cell, then read binding_pass for all three rows.
Expect True, False, False: changing the load or command invalidates this evidence binding.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L0–L1; cells classroom-002 and classroom-004.
note: Treat this first check as a content-consistency test, not a physical feasibility test. The first row keeps the request and command unchanged. The next two rows change a request field or command field. A failed binding requires fresh evidence, but does not prove the changed action is infeasible. A matching hash does not authenticate a sensor.
caption: Actual executed notebook output; source cell classroom-004. Fresh numerical calculation unless explicitly marked archived.

title: Use the same cycle in every case
points: Predict → run the default → read the result → change one input → rerun.
Finish by naming the permitted next step and the evidence that supports it.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L0–L1; cells classroom-002 and classroom-004.
note: Pause before showing each output. Ask pairs to write one sentence predicting the change, then compare it with the calculated result. Keep the input values and evidence together. Change only one parameter in the first experiment.
caption: Teaching diagram of the model or check used at this notebook step.

title: Keep a short experiment record
points: Record the cell label and parameter value you changed.
Record one result, its model scope and your next decision: continue, recheck or HOLD.
note: Participants can add a text cell below an output or use paper notes; no extra software is needed. Each pair should finish with one changed-input experiment that another person can repeat. Explain the result and one limit on the claim. The three cases use different networks and do not form a single utility deployment study.
